To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we replicated a body fat QTL in the RGS7 gene region on chromosome 1q in African-American women and in a meta-analysis of African-American and European-American women; and 2) we report for the first time moderate evidence of association of body fat with a SNP in PLD5, a gene involved in lipid signaling pathways, in African-American and European- American women.
we identified a novel body mass index quantitative trait locus (QTL) on chromosome 1q that is shared between European American and African American women.
we have replicated the association between the RGS7 gene and body fat, and we have identified PLD5 as a new body fat gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the genes and the genetic variants responsible for the susceptibility to obesity.
the study of obesity and related phenotypes in women of reproductive age, a population that is understudied.
the identification of genetic determinants of obesity and its associated traits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our study has identified a region of interest on human chromosome 13 for the genetic control of obesity.
RGS7 is a putative candidate gene for body fat in the human population.
RGS7 is a promising candidate gene for body fat in humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we report evidence of association for the RGS7 locus and body fat in African Americans, a finding that has not been reported in the literature to date.
the present findings support a role of RGS7 in the regulation of body fat and that this role might be shared between populations with European and African ancestry.

the RGS7 locus is a putative body-fat QTL that is associated with obesity-related traits in both African and European American populations and that this association is independent of the effects of the nearby PLD5 gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the genetic architecture of complex traits is highly heterogeneous among populations and that the use of reference panels from different populations is essential to identify the genetic factors underlying complex phenotypes.
the RGS7 gene is a promising candidate for obesity and that it is likely to harbor a functional variant(s) that may be involved in the regulation of body fat.
RGS7 is a promising candidate for further studies of obesity and body fat regulation.
